text.title: Poetry Project Setup — Failure Modes
text.summary: 7 antipatterns observed when python-poetry-setup is mis-applied, each with symptom, root cause, and concrete fix.

antipattern.description: ^2.0 dependency constraints in a publishable library.
antipattern.reason: Root cause: Users locked to 2.x even if 3.x is compatible. Fix: Use >=2.0,<3 for libraries; reserve caret for applications.
Root cause: Each install resolves differently; reproducibility gone. Fix: Commit the lockfile.
Root cause: Two sources of truth; drift inevitable. Fix: Pick one; if Poetry, delete requirements.txt or regenerate it from poetry export.
Root cause: Production install pulls in dev tooling. Fix: Move to [tool.poetry.group.dev.dependencies].

antipattern.description: Bare `poetry update` run on a shared repo — a massive lockfile diff, another developer's staged resolution overwritten, and a merge conflict on every subsequent push.
antipattern.reason: Root cause: `poetry update` treated like `git pull`, as a routine refresh rather than a deliberate version bump. Fix: `poetry update <pkg>` to bump one package; write the rule into CONTRIBUTING.md so it survives the next contributor.

antipattern.description: `poetry install` in the final Docker production stage — image over 200MB, with the Poetry runtime and often the dev deps shipped to production.
antipattern.reason: Root cause: A single-stage Dockerfile copy-pasted from a quickstart. Fix: Multi-stage — the builder exports requirements.txt, the final stage runs `pip install`. Typically drops 100-150MB.

antipattern.description: Broad Python constraint `python = ">=3.8"` — the solver runs roughly 10x slower and any conflict surfaces as a cryptic message about a version the project never targeted.
antipattern.reason: Root cause: Habit carried over from older tooling, where a wide range was how you stayed compatible. Fix: Pin tight — `python = "^3.11"`. The solver speeds up and conflict messages become readable.
